Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme of finite type over a field <MATH_0002>, and let <MATH_0003>
be a group scheme of finite type over <MATH_0004> which acts on <MATH_0005>.
Then the dimension of the quotient stack <MATH_0006> is equal to
<MATH_0007>. In particular, the dimension of the classifying
stack <MATH_0008> is <MATH_0009>. Thus the dimension of an algebraic
stack can be a negative integer, in contrast to what happens for schemes
or algebraic spaces.
